rv.q: Michael Grandage could hardly have made a better start to his five-show West End season than with this joyous revival of Peter Nichols's 1977 play with music.
Virtually the entire company turn in performances that show a discreet awareness of hinterland for their characters and the play as a whole
Privates on Parade may look safe but actually it's subtly unsettling.
The first season from the newly formed Michael Grandage Company starts brightly with this Seventies treat.
Dominic Cooke's excellent cast, including Emma Fielding and Stuart McQuarrie, are teasing and riveting.
Michael Grandage’s beautifully tragicomic production sneaks up on audiences unawares to deliver a surprise punch.

cn.t: Critics hail this revival as a joyous triumph, with Simon Russell Beale's drag turn earning particular praise. Grandage's production deftly blends comedy, parody, and postwar politics into a warm, extravagant package.
